meaning: One recorded attempt at the task, from start to finish.
An episode recorded while a person drives the arm, used as training data.
Supervised learning on (observation, action) pairs from demonstrations: the network is trained to output the action the person took for each observation.
The person (or controller) whose demonstrations the policy is trained to copy.
A small mistake moves the robot to a situation the demonstrations never showed, where the policy errs more, so the error feeds itself.
The number of decisions a policy takes in one task.
In the compounding-error bound, the probability that the policy disagrees with the expert on one decision, measured on situations the expert visited.
A run of the next k actions predicted from one observation and played in order before the policy looks again.
A 2023 imitation policy: a transformer that reads camera images and joint angles and outputs a whole chunk of actions in one forward pass.
An experiment that changes one setting and holds the rest fixed, to measure what that setting contributes.
The mean absolute difference between predicted and recorded values.
Asking the policy on every tick so chunks overlap, then averaging the overlapping predictions for smoother motion, at one forward pass per tick.
One cluster of valid answers; a task that can be done in two distinct ways has two modes.
Said of demonstrations whose good answers form several separate groups; unrelated to models that take images and text.
The output part of a network when it draws one sample from a set of good answers in place of returning a single best answer.
A model trained to rebuild its input through a small random vector; ACT uses it to keep different ways of doing a task apart.
A policy that starts from a chunk of random noise and removes predicted noise over many iterations until an action chunk remains.
One round in which the network predicts the noise in the current chunk and part of it is subtracted.
A sampling method for diffusion models that skips iterations, so fewer network passes are needed at inference.
A way to turn noise into a sample by training a network to output the direction from noise to data and following that direction in a few steps.
The network's answer, for every possible noisy chunk, to which way each number should move and how fast.
Progress through the sampling, from 0 (pure noise) to 1 (finished chunk); it all passes inside one policy call and is separate from the robot's clock.
A short straight step along the current velocity, after which the velocity is asked for again.
A robot model from Physical Intelligence that produces action chunks by flow matching; section 5 covers it.
Writing an action chunk as discrete tokens so a language model can predict them one at a time.
An action tokeniser that compresses a chunk with a cosine transform and byte-pair encoding before the language model predicts it.
Rewrites a signal as a sum of cosine waves, so a smooth motion needs only a few numbers.
A compressor that repeatedly merges pairs of symbols that occur often; text tokenisers use it.
A standard image network; ACT in LeRobot uses it to turn each camera image into feature vectors.
